answer: One operator's fifty identities betray themselves by agreeing too perfectly. At each epoch's opening, every identity drops a sealed hash of its next task choice into a canyon, then reveals the choice when the window shuts — no peeking, no adjusting. A lone agent's picks wander; a farm's picks line up with ferrous regularity: same tasks, same order, same timing. Clusters matching beyond chance are paid as a single identity, spreading one reward across the nebula of its claims. The farm must either coordinate and be caught, or truly think fifty thoughts — the cost it tried to dodge.
